title: Israel expands ground operations in Gaza amid communications blackout
body:
On the night of Friday 27 October 2023, the Israel Defense Forces announced that they were expanding ground operations inside Gaza after several nights of limited raids. The military said its air force was striking underground targets very significantly and that it had struck more than 250 Hamas targets in the preceding 24 hours, including tunnels, command centres and rocket launch positions. Internet and telephone services collapsed across the Gaza Strip during the escalation.

US and Israeli officials told ABC News that the incursion was not the large-scale offensive that Israel had threatened for three weeks, and the IDF said it was not the major operation expected. Defence Minister Yoav Gallant said a long, difficult ground offensive was coming and that dismantling Hamas's tunnel network would take a long time. Earlier that night, IDF infantry, armour and engineers had carried out a limited raid near Shejaiya in eastern Gaza City and withdrew after several hours, and naval commandos conducted a raid from the sea in southern Gaza.

The IDF said at least 233 people had been taken to Gaza on 7 October, and that four had been released. Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry reported more than 7,000 deaths, a figure that could not be independently verified, while Israel said it had killed about 1,500 Hamas fighters inside Israel on and after 7 October. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later described the entry of more ground forces as the second stage of the war.
